name: How early should I bring in a commercial general contractor?

mainEntity.name: At what stage should a Los Angeles owner involve a general contractor in a commercial project?
mainEntity.text: At what stage should a Los Angeles owner involve a general contractor in a commercial project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bringing in a contractor early can save a project from expensive redesign. During concept and schematic planning, a commercial general contractor can flag constructability problems, likely permit triggers, budget risks, and long-lead items. Early input is especially helpful in Los Angeles-area cities where review steps and inspection coordination can affect the opening date. If the contractor is only brought in after the design is complete, they may have to price around problems instead of helping avoid them. Owners should involve the contractor early if the project has tight timing, an older building, or a space that must stay occupied during construction. Early collaboration also improves the accuracy of the bid and reduces change orders later.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best time to involve a commercial general contractor is during early planning, before drawings are finished and before pricing assumptions are locked in. Early input helps identify permit risks, constructability issues, and budget problems before they become expensive changes. Late involvement usually means more redesign and more surprises.
